private_notes.observations: No prior rate cards or hour allocations are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate above cost, then use future rate cards and allocated hours to estimate how pricing affects our profit and adjust accordingly.

private_notes.observations: No rate cards or allocation outcomes are available yet. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive margin, then adjust future rates based on observed panel rates, allocated hours, and quarterly profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate versus Birchwood Hale’s $325 produced 663 hours and $99,450 profit. One quarter does not establish how allocation responds to price changes.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate modestly to test whether higher margin outweighs any loss of hours. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $325 rate was below Arden & Cole’s $350 rate and yielded 1,093 hours and $136,637 in profit. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how allocation responds to price changes.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate modestly while remaining below the competitor. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Q2’s $25 rate increase coincided with a drop from 663 to 522 allocated hours and lower quarterly profit, even as Birchwood Hale raised its rate from $325 to $335.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate to $350 to recover hours while retaining a $150 hourly margin. Compare the resulting allocation and profit with Q1 and Q2 before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: Q2 hours rose from 1,093 to 1,162 and reported profit rose from $136,637 to $156,807 after our rate increased from $325 to $335. Arden & Cole raised its rate from $350 to $375, widening our price advantage.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate moderately to $350 while remaining $25 below Arden & Cole's latest published rate. Track the effect on allocated hours and profit before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $350, profit rose from about $99,450 in Q1 to $126,696 in Q3 as Birchwood Hale's rate rose to match ours. The $375 rate in Q2 yielded lower profit, though quarterly demand may also have changed.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $350 for Q4 to preserve the strong allocation observed at rate parity. Reassess after seeing Q4 hours and Birchwood Hale's rate; avoid attributing all allocation changes to price when demand may vary.

private_notes.observations: At $350, matching Arden & Cole’s rate in Q3, our allocated hours fell to 845 and profit to $126,696. Our highest quarterly profit so far was at $335, when our rate was $40 below theirs, though allocation may also have varied for other reasons.
private_notes.plan: Set $335 to restore a competitive price while preserving a $135 hourly margin. Monitor allocated hours and profit; do not assume the competitor’s rate or Meridian’s demand will remain unchanged.

private_notes.observations: At $350, quarterly profit has been $99,450–$126,696, exceeding the $91,334 earned at $375. Q4 hours fell from Q3 as Birchwood Hale's rate dropped from $350 to $335, though demand may also have changed.
private_notes.plan: Keep the $350 rate. The observed gain in hours at that rate outweighs the higher margin achieved at $375. Reassess after another quarter rather than overreacting to uncertain demand changes.

private_notes.observations: At $335, quarterly profit was approximately $157,000 when Arden & Cole charged $375 and $134,000 when it charged $350. Matching Arden & Cole at $350 yielded lower profit, though quarterly demand also varies.
private_notes.plan: Maintain a competitive rate and monitor whether the additional hours from pricing below Arden & Cole offset the smaller hourly margin. Avoid drawing strong conclusions from four quarters of variable allocations.

private_notes.observations: At $350 against Birchwood Hale’s $335, we received 736 hours and earned $110,386 in each of Q4 and Q5. Our $375 rate in Q2 produced lower profit, though demand may also have differed.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $350 given two stable quarters at this rate. Reassess if the competing rate or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At Arden & Cole's $350 rate, our $325 rate produced slightly higher profit than $335 or $350, though allocations may vary across quarters. The $335 rate performed best when Arden & Cole charged $375.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to test whether the additional hours from a modest price advantage outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after observing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $350, profit ranged from $99,450 to $126,696 as Birchwood Hale’s rate varied from $325 to $350. The sole $375 quarter produced lower profit ($91,334). Birchwood Hale charged $325 in Q6.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $350. It has consistently outperformed the observed $375 outcome, and there is insufficient evidence that a lower rate would increase profit. Reassess after seeing Q7 hours and the rate card.

private_notes.observations: With Arden & Cole at $350, our $325 rate earned $136,637, compared with $134,105 at $335 and $126,696 at $350. Q6 replicated the Q1 outcome at $325.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $320. The observed relationship between rate and allocated hours suggests it may improve profit slightly; reassess after seeing the allocation and competitor rate.

private_notes.observations: At $350, hours fell from 845 when Birchwood charged $350 to 627 when Birchwood charged $320. Our only $375 quarter produced lower profit than any $350 quarter. Birchwood’s rate has declined to $320.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to test whether a lower rate wins enough additional hours to offset the smaller margin. Compare next quarter’s profit and rate card before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: With Arden & Cole at $350, our profit was $137,087 at $320, $136,637 at $325, and $134,105 at $335. The modest reduction to $320 improved profit slightly.
private_notes.plan: Test $317, near the estimated profit-maximizing rate based on observed hours at Arden & Cole's $350 rate. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: The Q8 reduction to $325 increased allocated hours to 835, but profit was $104,313, below the $110,386 earned at $350 when Birchwood charged $335. Birchwood’s rate has declined to $317, making a $350 rate less attractive.
private_notes.plan: Test a further reduction to $300. Estimate whether the additional hours offset the lower margin, then adjust based on Q9 profit and Birchwood’s published rate.

private_notes.observations: With Arden & Cole at $350, rates of $320–$335 produced similar profits; $350 produced less. Arden & Cole lowered its rate to $325 in Q8, and our $317 rate yielded 979 hours and $114,578 profit.
private_notes.plan: Account for the competitor’s lower rate rather than relying on the earlier $350-rate observations. Lower our rate modestly to seek more hours while preserving a substantial margin; reassess after Q9.

private_notes.observations: Q9’s $300 rate won 1,024 hours but earned $102,351, less than Q8’s $104,313 at $325. Birchwood’s published rate fell from $317 to $310. Past results suggest a rate near $305 could preserve much of the volume gained in Q9 while improving the margin.
private_notes.plan: Set $305 for Q10. Compare the resulting profit and hours with Q9, and use Birchwood’s next published rate to reassess whether a modest increase or decrease is warranted.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole cut its rate from $350 to $325 in Q8 and $300 in Q9. Our Q9 rate of $310 yielded 838 hours and about $92,000 in profit, substantially less than earlier quarters. When Arden & Cole held at $350, lowering our rate generally increased hours, but the recent competitor cuts changed the economics.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 to match the latest competing rate while retaining a $100 hourly margin. Reassess after seeing the Q10 allocation and rate card; avoid assuming that further cuts will recover enough hours to increase profit.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood’s rate has fallen to $300. At our $305 rate in Q10, we earned $93,137; at $300 in Q9, when Birchwood charged $310, we earned $102,351. The lower competing rate makes Q9’s result an optimistic benchmark.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 to remain competitive without reducing the margin below $100 per hour. Compare Q11 hours and profit against Q10, then reassess using Birchwood’s published rate.

private_notes.observations: At $300 against Arden & Cole's $305, we earned $98,031. Earlier cuts coincided with falling competitor rates and lower profits, so further undercutting is not clearly beneficial.
private_notes.plan: Raise modestly to improve margin without moving far above the latest competing rate. Reassess both allocation and the competitor's next published rate before making another change.

private_notes.observations: At $300 with Birchwood at $315 in Q11, we earned $106,601. The $305 rate earned $93,137 in Q10 when Birchwood charged $300. Allocation varies substantially with the competing rate.
private_notes.plan: Keep a competitive $100-per-hour margin at $300. Reassess after seeing Q12 hours and Birchwood’s published rate; avoid sacrificing substantial volume for a small rate increase.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole has charged $300 in two of the last three quarters. At those rates, our $310–$315 rates earned about $91k–$92k per quarter; charging $300 when Arden charged $305 earned about $98k.
private_notes.plan: Reduce our rate modestly to improve our competitiveness while retaining margin. Reassess after the next allocation and published rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $300, recent quarterly profit has been approximately $98,000–$107,000. Birchwood’s rate fell from $315 to $305 last quarter, making a rate increase risky for allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Maintain a competitive rate and preserve volume while monitoring Birchwood’s next rate and our allocation.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole held its rate at $300 in Q11–Q12. At that competitor rate, our Q12 rate of $305 yielded 887 hours and approximately $93,137 profit. Recent results suggest a rate near $300 offers the best balance of margin and allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 this quarter. Compare the resulting hours and Arden & Cole’s next published rate card before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood’s rate has fallen to $300. Our $300 rate has maintained strong allocation, while recent increases above Birchwood’s rate generally reduced our hours.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300 to protect volume and profit. Reassess if Birchwood raises its rate or allocation changes materially.

private_notes.observations: With Arden & Cole at $300, our $300 rate yielded 937 hours and $93,662 profit in Q13. Our higher rates of $305–$315 earned less profit when Arden & Cole charged $300.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300. The estimated gain from a small cut is negligible, while a stable rate avoids encouraging further price competition. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has held at $300 for two quarters. At matched $300 rates, we received 937 hours and earned $93,662 each quarter. Raising our rate above Birchwood’s has historically reduced our allocation substantially.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300 while Birchwood remains at $300. Reassess if its rate or our allocation changes materially.

private_notes.observations: At matching $300 rates in Q13–Q14, we received 937 hours and earned approximately $93,662 per quarter. Recent deviations above $300 earned less when Arden & Cole charged $300.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300. A modest rate change offers little demonstrated profit improvement; reassess if the competing rate or allocation changes.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has held $300 for three quarters; at matching rates, our allocation has remained 937 hours and profit approximately $93,662 per quarter. Past rate changes suggest a modest increase above $300 would reduce hours enough to offset the higher margin.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 while the rival's rate and our allocation remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: At both firms' $300 rates, allocation and profit have been stable for three quarters at 937 hours and $93,662 per quarter. Prior small rate increases when Arden & Cole charged $300 reduced our profit.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 to preserve stable long-run profitability. Reassess if Arden & Cole changes its rate or our allocation shifts.

private_notes.observations: Both firms have held rates at $300 for four quarters, yielding us 937 hours and roughly $93,662 profit each quarter. Our highest profit in the recent history was about $104,313 at a $325 rate when Birchwood Hale charged $317.
private_notes.plan: Test a moderate increase to $325. Compare the resulting hours and profit with the stable $300 baseline, then reassess next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Both firms have held $300 for four quarters, with our allocation steady at about 937 hours and profit around $93,662 per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 to preserve the stable account economics. Reassess if Arden & Cole changes its rate or our allocated hours shift.

private_notes.observations: At matching $300 rates in Q13–Q16, profit was consistently $93,662 per quarter. Raising our rate to $325 in Q17 while Birchwood remained at $300 reduced profit to $87,052.
private_notes.plan: Return to $300. Monitor Birchwood's rate and our allocated hours; reconsider if its pricing changes.

private_notes.observations: At matching $300 rates, quarterly profit was about $93,662. When Arden & Cole charged $325 last quarter, holding $300 increased profit to $114,819. Earlier, a $317 rate against their $325 yielded $114,578.
private_notes.plan: Keep $300 this quarter. The observed gain from raising our rate against a $325 competitor is negligible, while a higher rate would expose us to lower allocated hours if Arden & Cole returns to $300. Reassess after the next rate card and allocation.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood has priced at $300 for six consecutive quarters. At matching $300, our profit has consistently been $93,662; raising to $325 in Q17 reduced profit to $87,052.
private_notes.plan: Maintain the stable $300 rate rather than risk lower profit from a price increase or provoke a prolonged price decline. Reassess if Birchwood changes its rate or allocated hours shift.

private_notes.observations: At a competing $300 rate, our $300 rate earned $93,662 repeatedly; increases to $305–$315 earned less. When Arden & Cole charged $325, our $300 rate earned $114,819.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300. It has performed well against both observed competitor rates, while increases have not improved profit. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At matching $300 rates, Arden & Cole has repeatedly received 937 hours and earned approximately $93,662 per quarter. Raising our rate to $325 while Birchwood stayed at $300 reduced profit to $87,052. Birchwood has held at $300 for seven consecutive quarters.
private_notes.plan: Keep the established $300 rate. Reassess if Birchwood changes its rate or Meridian's allocation shifts.

private_notes.observations: At $300, profit was approximately $93,662 when Arden & Cole charged $300 and $114,819 when it charged $325. Past increases above $300 generally produced lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 based on observed profit and allocation outcomes. Reassess if future results indicate a different rate would improve long-run profit.
